description:
The MCP bridge requests machine output only from leaves that declare their own `json` flag, so it would silently receive human output once `--json` becomes one global CLI flag. This makes the injection follow the schema's `global_options` as well.

## Background

`buildCliArgs(cmdPath, args, cmdDef)` in `mcp-server/lib/cli-executor.js` computes `hasJsonFlag` from `cmdDef.flags` and appends `--json` only when it is true. `mcp-server/lib/tool-generator.js` turns every leaf flag into a tool input property, which is why `json` is a tool property today. The CLI schema printed by `jit --schema` lists globally accepted flags once in `global_options` (today `quiet`, `schema`, `help`, `version`) and keeps them out of each leaf's `flags`. The CLI is moving `--json` to a single `global = true` flag on `Cli`; after that no leaf carries `json`. Supporting both shapes lets the bridge keep working across the cutover.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `buildCliArgs` appends exactly one `--json` when the leaf declares a `json` flag or the schema's `global_options` declares `json`, and appends none when neither does.
- [hard] REQ-02: A global `json` option adds no `json` input property to generated tools, while leaf flags still map to tool properties as before.
- [hard] REQ-03: Unit tests in `mcp-server/test-unit.js` exercise injection against a schema with per-leaf `json` flags and against one with only a global `json` option, and the existing injection and no-duplication tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

How `global_options` reaches `buildCliArgs` (an argument or state held by the executor) is an implementation choice.

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
title: MCP bridge injects --json from the schema's global options
